text:
alex: Heads-up — noticed ~12% p95 latency jump on the streaming API in canary after last night's deploy. CI perf/reg shows SSE endpoints tailing up. cc @maria @sam

ci-bot: perf/regression detected: streaming_latency_p95 increased from 210ms -> 235ms (+12%). Suspected culprit: merge 5832f3a (feature/tool-calls-protocol).

jordan: Ran pprof on canary; hot paths look like json.Marshal and net write/flush syscalls.

maria: My local traces match — the new tool-calling wrapper adds an extra struct and we end up marshalling twice in some code paths. Also middleware now aggregates SSE events.

sam: Can you paste the flamegraph / pprof dump?

alex: Flamegraph here: https://perf.re/redwood/fg/1749001234
pprof top snippet:
```
64.1ms  30.2%  json.Marshal
48.3ms  22.7%  net/http.(*response).flush
```

lee: The streaming middleware changed to batch small events to reduce syscalls, but that increases latency for low-frequency streams — SSEs wait longer to hit buffer threshold before flush.

maria: Proposed fix: add immediateFlush flag for latency-sensitive routes (/_stream endpoints) and remove redundant Marshal in the tool-runner path. This should restore p95 without reverting big changes.

sam: Can we hotfix by toggling the aggregation middleware off for /v1/stream in the routing table? Or enable TCP_NODELAY / explicit flush after each event? Tradeoff: more syscalls.

jordan: I toggled the middleware off in a canary and reran perf — p95 dropped to 208ms (back to baseline). Patch ready: revert aggregation in streaming-middleware + dedupe marshal in tool-runner. Opening PR now.

alex: Perf CI run queued: https://ci.redwood/1749001234 — if green we can roll forward, otherwise revert 5832f3a.

ci-bot: perf CI: job 4421 started.

maria: Also adding a unit test to assert single marshal and a microbenchmark for flush interval so this doesn't regress silently.

sam: :thumbsup: If revert takes time, temporary config change per-route (immediateFlush = true) is low-risk. Also consider emitting a small keepalive comment `:\n` to force flush on some SSE clients.

lee: FYI we should check if kernel selection / batching heuristics in runtime amplify this under high concurrency — even though root cause is protocol flush frequency. Adding ENGRT follow-up.

alex: Filing ENGRT-3215 to evaluate kernel scheduling impact on small-write tail latency and link this thread. Thanks all — will monitor CI and coordinate rollout.
